claims.statement: Rebuilding clears changes outside /workspaces while preserving changes inside that directory, including the repository/template clone, according to the pinned note. Rebuild persistence is not hosted backup or protection from whole-codespace deletion. This loss boundary qualifies prior rebuild guidance; no rebuild or data removal occurred and the directory-structure link remains separate.

The source recommends rebuilding to check configuration changes before commit and describes a recovery container after failure for continued adjustments. Its phrase about expected operation is procedural intent, not proof that rebuilding alone verifies all functional/security requirements or a successful recovery. No runtime validation occurred.

The recovery procedure views creation logs, edits devcontainer.json to fix identified errors and rebuilds. It also describes the CLI rebuild route for externally changed configuration with interactive target selection. The included recovery-mode fragment is separately reviewed here; screenshot pixels and actual safe target/custody remain separate. No CLI command, logs or rebuild executed.

When configuration changes cause a container error, the pinned fragment describes recovery mode and an error message. This conditional behavior is not proof of data recovery, arbitrary-error coverage or a presently healthy environment.

Suggested PR changes are optional and become author commits only if the author agrees; the procedure selects lines, edits a suggestion and adds a comment. A suggestion/comment is not review approval, merged change or authorization to message externally; screenshot pixels remain separate and no comment was posted.

The isolated save step depends on surrounding context and means saving changes, not committing, pushing, backing up or proving effective configuration. No persistent remote custody follows from this fragment alone.

Same-name secrets at multiple levels use the lowest-level secret; the explicit example gives repository-level precedence over organization-level. Do not infer every unspecified level ordering or actual resolved secret value from this example. No secret value was acquired or changed.

Codespaces secret names permit ASCII letters, digits and underscores, prohibit spaces, a leading digit and the GITHUB_ prefix, compare case-insensitively and require uniqueness within the creation level. These are source-defined naming constraints, not proof of secret storage/access safety or implemented local validation; no credentials were read or created.
